statement.p: Some airlines have restrictions on the size of items of luggage that passengers are allowed to take with them. Suppose that one has a rule that the sum of the length, width and height of any piece of luggage must be less than or equal to 234 cm. A passenger wants to take a box of the maximum allowable volume. If the length and width are to be equal, what should the dimensions be?
In this case, what is the volume?
If the length is be twice the width, what should the dimensions be?
In this case, what is the volume?

static.solution:
L, w and h, respectively. Then the volume of the box is V = Lwh. The sum L + w + h = 234, and, for the first part, we know that L = w. Thus 2w + h = 234, so h = 234 - 2w, and the volume equation becomes V = Lwh = w\cdot w\cdot(234 - 2w) = 234\cdot w^2 - 2w^3. The domain for w is 0\le w\le 234.
Critical points are where \frac{dV}{dw} = 2\cdot 234\cdot w - 6\cdot w^2 = 0, so w = 0 or w = 78. The global maximum must occur either at this point or at the end points. V(78) > 0 while V(0) = V(234) = 0, so the global maximum is at L=w=78, in which case h=78 as well. The volume is then V = 78^3 = 474552 {\rm cm}^3.
If L = 2w, 2w + w + h = 234, so V = (2w)(w)(234 - 3w) = 468 w^2 - 6 w^3. Proceeding as before, we find w = 52, L = 104 and h = 78, so that V = 421824.
